title: Midnight Sun Integrators hybrid on-ramp discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Midnight Sun Integrators to scope a hybrid on-ramp: private control plane + on-prem GPU nodes in Nordics, routing policies, security requirements and pilot success metrics. Agreed next steps: share deployment checklist, schedule week-long benchmark window, internal alignment on licensing model.
next_steps: Redwood to share private deployment checklist and SSO/SAML integration guide (Evan) by 2028-02-18
Customer to provide VM topology and sample throughput targets (Anya) by 2028-02-21
Schedule 1-week benchmark with a small model and 2x A100-equivalent nodes (Maya/Evan) w/in 2 weeks
action_items: Evan Brooks: Send partner onboarding deck and Private deployment checklist (due 2028-02-18)
Maya Patel: Draft benchmark plan + data handling SOPs (due 2028-02-20)
Anya Lind: Share network topology and expected qps/p95 targets (due 2028-02-21)
Hana Kvale: List audit requirements (SOC2 control gaps) and bring any legal red flags (due 2028-02-22)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-02-14 09:30 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Evan, Maya, Priya, Tom (Redwood) — Soren, Anya, Diego, Hana (Midnight Sun)

Auto-summary: initial partner discovery to assess feasibility of Redwood Private control plane integrating with MSI on-prem GPU pools in Norway/Sweden. Main concerns: KMS integration, data residency, routing/failover, and commercial split for channel/reseller.

00:00:03 Evan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros — um Soren you wanna kick off? 
00:00:12 Soren Bjork: Yeah thanks Evan, hey all. I'm Soren, CTO at Midnight Sun Integrators, we do telco edge infra across scans — sorry Scandinavia — Scandinavian sites for low-latency inference. We wanted to talk about on-ramp options to Redwood, partner flow, and how we could resell or embed the inference runtime with our managed service.
00:00:38 Maya Patel: Great, thanks. I'll surface the high-level options: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and the Private/VPC model which usually fits SI on-prem scenarios. Today we wanted to focus on Private and hybrid — the on-prem GPU onramp. 
00:00:56 Anya Lind: Yep our primary ask is: we need a private control plane that doesn't send PII to public clouds, keys are customer-managed, and we need predictable latency for 99th percentile. Also curious about how routing works if your hosted capacity is saturated — do you hand off to a partner site? 
00:01:17 Evan Brooks: Right. So Redwood Private can run with a customer-managed control plane; KMS/HSM integrations are supported for key material. For routing, we have policy-driven smart routing — you can prefer local GPU pools, fall back to lower-cost regions, or to quantized variants. In partner setups we've also done direct routing to SI-managed nodes. 
00:01:40 Diego Ramos: Quick Q — when you say "KV cache", do you mean a shared cache between control plane and on-prem nodes? how does cold-start look? we care about warm-up times. 
00:01:52 Maya Patel: Good callout. The KV cache stays local to the serving nodes; the control plane orchestrates stateful stickiness for long-lived sessions. cold-start depends on model size and whether you pre-warm. For a 13B-ish open model you'll see longer cold starts; for GPU with low-latency SLOs we recommend pre-warming key workers or using model sharding with warmed KV. (murmur) sorry — model sharding and pinned allocations.
00:02:24 Hana Kvale: From compliance, SOC2 and detailed audit logs are non-negotiable, plus we need retention config. Do you ingest logs into our SIEM or do you host them? 
00:02:35 Priya Nair: We support audit forwarders — you can ship audit logs to your S3 or to a SIEM via our connector, and retention is configurable at per-tenant level. For Private deployments logs can remain inside customer network. 
00:02:51 Soren Bjork: On the reseller side — how do margins and billing work if we bring capacity? like if MSI sells a managed inference offering with Redwood as underlying runtime, is that allowed? 
00:03:04 Tom Wu: We have partner/reseller programs and channel pricing for Dedicated/Private. Typically there's a partner discount and you can white-label via our partner agreement. We'll follow up with legal/partner program details. (Evan nods) 
00:03:20 Anya Lind: Network: our sites are mostly behind NAT and a few MPLS links. How do you secure control plane traffic — outbound-only? do we need public ingress? 
00:03:31 Maya Patel: For Private we can do an outbound-only control channel, or a customer-managed VPN/peering. In some air-gapped cases we ship an appliance and the control plane is customer-hosted. We'll need ports/opening only for orchestration and KV synchronization, but no payload tokens leave the customer environment when properly configured. 
00:03:55 Diego Ramos: Do you support HSMs? we run a vault cluster using AWS KMS and an HSM for on-prem. 
00:04:03 Evan Brooks: Yes, KMS integrations and HSM-backed key wrap are supported. We have docs on KMS connectors. I'll share the exact integration notes after. 
00:04:12 Soren: Good. Performance: what's the baseline throughput we can expect per A100+32gb equivalent node for streaming chat? p50/p95? 
00:04:24 Maya Patel: Ballpark — depending on model and quantization: for a 7B optimized model on A100 equiv, you might see 30-60 reqs/sec with 50-300ms p50 and 200-700ms p95 for short contexts. For long contexts and higher concurrency you want dedicated pinned workers and batching. We should run a small benchmark to get concrete numbers for your prompts. 
00:04:50 Anya: That variance is big — our customers require SLA 99% < 300ms; is that achievable? 
00:04:57 Maya Patel: If you pin workers and keep prompt lengths low and avoid high batching, yes 99% < 300ms is feasible at small scale. At scale you trade throughput for latency. We'll propose a config with small batch size, pre-warmed workers, and priority queues. 
00:05:15 Hana: Audit again — do you provide change history for model rollouts and who triggered them? we need that for compliance. 
00:05:22 Priya: Yes, rollout history, model versioning, and who initiated can be audited; we include hooks for SSO + RBAC so actions are traceable. 
00:05:33 Soren: Great. On the integration pattern: we want an onramp where MSI can manage GPU capacity behind our managed service and Redwood control plane either in our VPC or yours — we want to avoid double-billing and want clear cost attribution. How have others handled revenue split? 
00:05:50 Tom: Partners run two common models: 1) MSI hosts capacity and bills their customers; Redwood charges MSI a partner rate, MSI charges customers; or 2) Redwood hosts control plane and bills end customers while MSI gets a referral margin. We'll send partner commercial options and an example pricing sheet. 
00:06:08 Diego: For the pilot we propose 2 on-prem nodes in Oslo, reachable over VPN, and a week-long benchmark with our sample prompt set. We'd like to test fallback to a cloud model if local nodes fail. 
00:06:21 Maya: Sounds good; typical plan: 1) onboarding + infra checklist, 2) deploy agent/connector on your nodes, 3) run baseline workloads and gather perf/cost numbers, 4) iterate. We'll own step 2 and 3 with you. 
00:06:36 Soren: Do you have an appliance image? air-gapped play? 
00:06:40 Evan: Yes we offer an on-prem appliance image and an offline install path — used in highly regulated customers. There's also a lightweight agent for less sealed networks. 
00:06:49 Anya: Security — what about data residency and in-memory scrubbing? we get nervous about PII. 
00:06:55 Priya: We support per-request data tagging and auto-scrub on write, and memory zeroization on decommission. We'll document the guarantees. 
00:07:05 Hana: Legal wants to see SOC2 and any penetration test reports. 
00:07:09 Evan: We'll share SOC2 report and the latest pen test summary under an NDA. I'll send the security packet. 
00:07:16 (brief cross-talk) 
00:07:25 Diego: A couple of nitty gritty questions — what's your preferred telemetry ship? we use Prometheus/Grafana locally. 
00:07:33 Maya: We export metrics to Prometheus and provide dashboards for per-route latency and cost. There's also a tracing hook for spans. 
00:07:44 Soren: Great. Any blockers we see? network, keys, commercial ok. 
00:07:49 Evan: On the commercial side, we need to align on who signs the MSA and whether MSI will be a reseller or a sub-processor. We'll coordinate legal. 
00:07:58 Anya: Ok can we do a quick recap and confirm next steps? 
00:08:02 Evan: Sure. recap: Redwood will share partner/Private deployment checklist, SSO/SAML and KMS integration notes, SOC2 + pen test summary (under NDA). Redwood will propose a benchmark plan and pricing options for channel/reseller. MSI will share network topology, sample prompt set, and target SLAs. We'll aim to schedule the benchmark w/in 2 weeks. Anything else? 
00:08:29 Soren: Also please include example partner contract language for margin splits. 
00:08:33 Tom: noted, will add partner contract sample. 
00:08:36 Hana: I'll assemble audit and legal asks and send to Evan. 
00:08:40 Evan: Perfect. we'll follow up by email and drop links to the docs. 

00:09:05 Closing notes — references shared in chat: partner onboarding deck (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/midnight-sun/onramp), private-deploy-checklist.pdf, KMS-integration.md. Action items agreed. Thanks all. 

Transcript imperfections: "KV cache" was sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash" and "Redwood Private" came out as "Redwood dedicate" in a few places due to audio glitch. There were a couple of overlaps during Q&A causing partial word drops.
